speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, could you please tell me more about the yellowish coloring you're experiencing and if you've noticed any changes in your urine or stool? Also, have you been feeling any abdominal pain or nausea?

speaker: Patient
text: 20-year-old male. The patient was previously healthy and has been brought to the emergency department due to agitation over the past 24 hours. Family members have noticed a yellowish coloring of his skin and eyes over the past week. The patient has a history of occasional cocaine and ecstasy use, and drinks alcohol socially on weekends. The patient also admits to high-risk sexual behaviors without using appropriate protection.

speaker: Doctor

text: The normal hepatitis antibody panel rules out acute viral hepatitis, so we need to look at other causes for this severe liver injury and coagulopathy. Do you have any history of acetaminophen use, or have you been exposed to any mushrooms, industrial chemicals, or herbal supplements recently?

text: The agitation and confusion, combined with severe liver injury and coagulopathy but negative viral hepatitis markers, strongly suggest acute liver failure, possibly from toxin ingestion.
